blockMcqs.question: What is the right way to reason about cloud cost?
options: Minimize raw dollar cost above all else
Maximize raw performance regardless of price
Optimize performance-per-dollar
Ignore it until the finance team flags it
blockMcqs.explanation: A box twice as fast for 1.5x the price is the better buy.

blockMcqs.question: Which cost bucket grows with user traffic and region boundaries?
options: Storage held
Network egress
Reserved compute
Per-operation read fees
blockMcqs.explanation: Bytes leaving the provider or crossing regions are billed per GB.

blockMcqs.question: Why does moving a byte cost more than holding it?
options: Disks are scarcer than network links
Egress is taxed by regulators
Storage is subsidized by compute
The provider's marginal cost lives in network links
blockMcqs.explanation: Fiber, routers, and peering links are where the real expense sits.

blockMcqs.question: How does storage cost behave over time?
options: Elastic — rises and falls with requests
A ratchet — it almost only grows
Flat once the table is provisioned
Falls automatically as data ages
blockMcqs.explanation: Without deletes or tiering, written data accumulates monotonically.

blockMcqs.question: Capacity planning should size the fleet against what?
options: Average traffic to save money
Historical peak plus headroom
The single busiest second ever seen
Whatever autoscaling chooses at runtime
blockMcqs.explanation: Average sizing fails whenever load exceeds the mean, which is half the time.

blockMcqs.question: Which workload best fits spot/preemptible instances?
options: A primary stateful database
A fault-tolerant stateless batch job
The always-on steady baseline
A latency-critical checkout path
blockMcqs.explanation: Spot can be reclaimed in minutes, so only interruptible work survives it.

blockMcqs.question: A lifecycle policy on object storage primarily does what?
options: Caches hot data closer to users
Reserves compute for steady load
Ages cooling data into cheaper tiers
Replicates data across all regions
blockMcqs.explanation: Rarely-read bytes move to cold storage, trading restore speed for cost.

blockMcqs.question: What is the main downside of reserved instances?
options: They can be reclaimed with two minutes' notice
They cost more than on-demand per hour
They lock you in for the full term
They cannot be autoscaled at all
blockMcqs.explanation: A 3-year commitment on a workload you kill early is pure waste.

blockMcqs.question: Why did Netflix build Open Connect inside ISP networks?
options: To shard its user database geographically
To avoid cloud egress on video bytes
To run analytics on spot instances
To meet regional data-residency laws
blockMcqs.explanation: Serving from a box at the ISP keeps video off expensive egress links.

blockMcqs.question: A box at 8% CPU has high latency. First move?
options: Provision a larger instance immediately
Diagnose the code, queries, or contention
Switch the fleet to spot instances
Add more storage to the volume
blockMcqs.explanation: Idle CPU means size isn't the bottleneck; sizing up just bills forever.
